output.title: Attribution starts with one source field you can trust
output.body:
If you care about attribution, the first question is not which dashboard to buy. It is whether your leads already pass through one place where source can be recorded consistently: a form, CRM, email reply, or sales record. If the answer is no, attribution is a data-plumbing problem first, and an AI problem never.

For a small business owner, the useful check is simple. When a lead turns into a customer, can you trace it back to one channel or campaign without guessing? If you need memory, a spreadsheet note, or whatever someone typed last Tuesday, the measurement is shaky.

The next step is a small manual spot-check. Pick a short recent set of closed deals, look back to the original trail, and compare that source with what your CRM says. A small sample does not prove the whole system is right; it tells you whether the control is real or just decorative. Controls have a way of looking confident right up until you ask them a question.

If the source field is blank, inconsistent, or routinely overwritten, fix the input rule before adding AI or more analytics. Once source data is reliable, then you can decide whether lead scoring, channel-based replies, or another automation is worth testing. Before that, you are just measuring noise more neatly.
